title: Prenatal exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals in relation to thyroid hormone levels in infants - a Dutch prospective cohort study.
ehr_evidence: information on T4 levels in heel prick blood spots was obtained through the neonatal screening programme in the Netherlands
summary: A Dutch prospective mother-child cohort study (LINC study) of 83 mother-child pairs examining associations between prenatal exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals (DDE, DEHP metabolites, HCB, PCB-153, PFOS, PFOA) measured in cord plasma/breast milk and neonatal total T4 levels from the national neonatal screening programme
key_findings: In girls, the highest quartile of total DDE exposure (>107.50 ng/L) was associated with increased T4 of +24.8 nmol/L (95% CI 0.79, 48.75; p=0.043) versus the lowest quartile in the fully adjusted model
In girls, the highest quartile of PFOA exposure (>1200 ng/L) was associated with increased T4 of +38.6 nmol/L (95% CI 13.34, 63.83; p=0.004) versus the lowest quartile in the fully adjusted model

In boys, the second quartile of PFOS exposure was associated with lower T4 in the crude model (-22.1 nmol/L, 95% CI -38.75 to -5.48; p=0.010) but this association was attenuated and no longer significant after full adjustment
In boys, the second quartile of PFOA exposure was associated with lower T4 in the crude model (-20.3 nmol/L, 95% CI -37.29 to -3.24; p=0.021) but attenuated after adjustment
No significant associations with T4 were observed for the DEHP metabolites (MECPP, MEHHP, MEOHP) or PCB-153
captured_features: Total T4 (nmol/L) from neonatal screening heel prick blood spots
DDE in cord plasma and breast milk
DEHP metabolites (MECPP, MEHHP, MEOHP) in cord plasma
data_source_type: biospecimen (cord plasma/breast milk assays) linked to national neonatal screening registry
population: Dutch mother-child cohort (LINC study) recruited from six midwifery clinics in Zwolle, Netherlands, 2011-2013; 83 mother-child pairs analysed; neonates/infants
exposure_domain: Endocrine disrupting chemicals (organochlorine pesticides/DDE, polychlorinated biphenyls/PCB-153, hexachlorobenzene, phthalates/DEHP metabolites, perfluorinated alkyl acids/PFOS and PFOA)
limitations: Small sample size (n=83) with reduced power after quartile and sex-specific stratification
No correction for multiple testing, raising risk of false-positive findings
Homogeneous population (all Dutch origin, majority highly educated) limits generalizability
DDE breast milk levels converted to cord blood using an external conversion factor
Not adjusted for time of heel prick sampling (4-7 days after birth)
Substantial loss of exposure data (51 of 148 children excluded due to insufficient/failed sample collection)
